summary: Converted the verbal pre-push library-seam audit into a mechanical check per CLAUDE_ROOT.md non-negotiable #5 ('Mechanism over prose. When a rule keeps getting missed, the fix is a check that fails — not another paragraph in this file'). New src/library-seam.test.ts walks every .ts/.tsx file under src/features, extracts function/class/const-arrow-assignment definitions via regex, and fails if any name overlaps a runtime export of tapit-attest. ALLOWLIST exists for intentional coincidences but is currently empty by design. Verified the check fails when it should by temporarily injecting an `envelopeId` collision in src/features/journal/__canary.ts — test surfaced the exact file path + name + ALLOWLIST guidance. Removed canary, re-ran clean. One commit (66637f1) on branch + main.

why.text: Operator: 'Fire up read Claude Md stay centered work on next task. Still working on netlify verify don't trust.' Re-read CLAUDE_ROOT.md fresh — non-negotiable #5 directly applies: the tapit-attest-integrity rule has been caught three times across autonomous-work blocks (entry-digest, anchor-attachment, useWalletIdentity reference), each by the verbal pattern that requires Carpenter attention. Doctrine literally says: when a rule keeps getting missed, add a check, not a paragraph. The name-collision subset of the rule is the dominant failure mode and is automatable; semantic-collision-without-name-overlap is rarer and still needs human attention. Single focused commit, mechanical, no operator-attention cost, preserved across future sessions.

outcome.tests_passing: 17/17 — 16 prior + 1 new library-seam test. Runtime ~13ms (negligible). tapit-attest unchanged.
outcome.notes: Commit 66637f1 on branch + main. No bundle impact (test file excluded from build). The 'don't trust verify' framing applied to the check itself — I deliberately injected a collision and confirmed the test detected it before removing the canary.

uncertainty: The regex for definitions is intentionally broad (matches function/class/const-arrow). Edge cases like destructured-then-reassigned imports or rebinding via `const { x } = lib` are NOT caught. If those become a real failure mode, the check can extend. For now the simple case covers the historical bugs.
next: Pausing at a clean stop. Library-seam check now runs on every `npm test` and on every CI pass. The five remaining follow-ups are non-blocking: multi-tab worker coordination, HEIC/WebP photo re-encode, bundle-budget audit, OTS fixture restoration, Tap-it-Attest-main.zip cleanup. v1 surface unchanged — still feature-complete.
